references.text: The Lord parted the Red Sea so that the Israelites could cross on dry ground, which Rahab refers to as one of the mighty wonders they had heard about.
Moses' song describes how the nations will hear of the Lord's mighty deeds and tremble, a prophecy fulfilled in Rahab's testimony.
The account of Israel's victory over Sihon, king of the Amorites, and Og, king of Bashan, which Rahab mentions as one reason why the people of Jericho were afraid.
Moses recounts the victory over Sihon, king of Heshbon, which Rahab refers to.
Moses recounts the victory over Og, king of Bashan, which Rahab mentions together with Sihon.
A reminder that the Lord caused the waters of the Red Sea to overwhelm the Egyptians, the same miracle Rahab testifies about.
Joshua explains that the Lord dried up the Jordan just as He did the Red Sea, so that all the peoples of the earth might know the Lord's power.
The Gibeonites repeat the same testimony as Rahab: that they have heard of the Lord's deeds, including the victories over Sihon and Og.
The psalm praises the Lord for the miracle at the Red Sea, the same miracle Rahab testifies about.
Praise to the Lord for parting the Red Sea and for the victories over Sihon and Og, the same events Rahab mentions.
Hebrews mentions Rahab's faith, which led her to welcome the spies and be spared, based on her knowledge of the Lord's deeds.
